headline: Amazon releases Mitra-v2, an open model for tabular data
dek: The weights are open on Hugging Face, per Amazon Science.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: The release
body: Amazon released Mitra-v2, an AI model that predicts values in tables, with open weights on Hugging Face, per Amazon Science.
It uses the Apache 2.0 license, and the package includes fine-tuning code (Amazon Science).

points.t: Reads labeled rows and predicts the rest.
Cuts columns in very wide tables.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Results
body: Per Amazon Science, Mitra-v2 leads standalone models on TabArena, with 51 datasets.
It beat Mitra-v1 on 32 of 33 datasets (Amazon Science).

items.t: Amazon already uses it in Connect (Amazon Science).
Above ten, it uses a tree (Amazon Science).
Blends eight versions by default (Amazon Science).

caption.hook: Amazon released Mitra-v2, an open AI model for predicting values in data tables.
body: Per Amazon Science, the weights are on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license, with classification and regression versions. The model reads labeled rows of a new table and predicts the rest, with no extra training, through in-context learning.

Amazon says Mitra-v2 was pretrained on synthetic tables with ten times more rows and about three times more columns than Mitra-v1. Per the company, it leads standalone models on TabArena and beat Mitra-v1 on 32 of 33 datasets. The Amazon Connect team already uses the model internally.
